transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jonas Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Eli Mercer (Sandbar Head of ML), Dana Zhou (Sandbar Platform), Rohit Patel (Sandbar Security), Maya Singh (Sandbar PM)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on success criteria, infra constraints, security review items, and next steps to start an activation pilot. Primary goals: confirm throughput/latency SLOs, pin down VPC/on-prem constraints, and share Redwood onboarding artifacts.

Topics:
- Production latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and cache policies
- Private vs dedicated deployment options and VPC networking
- Security questionnaire and KMS integration
- Pilot scope and timeline for a 2-week activation run

Action items (high level): see metadata field for owner/dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? I'll kick it off, I'm Ava with Redwood, I own the AE motion for Sandbar.
[00:10] Eli Mercer: Hey, Eli here. I'm head of ML at Sandbar, focusing on the ingestion and conversational features.
[00:15] Dana Zhou: Dana, platform engineering, taking point on network and infra.
[00:20] Rohit Patel: Rohit, security. We'll be looking at encryption and audit log needs.
[00:25] Maya Singh: Maya, PM on the product side — timeline and success metrics.
[00:30] Jonas Park: Jonas from CS, I'll be your onboarding contact and runbook shepherd.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Priya, solutions eng, I'll run the infra deep-dive and help with perf tuning.

[01:05] Ava Martinez: Awesome. Goal for today is to align on what a successful 2-week activation pilot looks like. We want to set success criteria, capture any blockers (security, network), and schedule follow-ups.
[01:20] Eli Mercer: For us success is basically two things: 1) sub-400ms median gen latency for 512-token prompts in production-like tests and 2) <15% token cost delta vs the bench we currently run.
[01:36] Priya Nair: Understood. A note — our fleet profiling typically measures tail p95 and p99, so we'll map median and tail to configs. If you have seq-length histogram that helps.
[01:50] Dana Zhou: We'll share real qps numbers but rough is 200 rps baseline with spikes to 800 for campaign events, mostly single-turn generation, some streaming.

[02:20] Jonas Park: Thanks. On deployment options we surfaced three possibilities in the docs: hosted Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity, and Redwood Private (VPC). Which are you leaning toward?
[02:35] Eli Mercer: We're leaning Dedicated for predictability but open to Private if we hit compliance constraints. We do have some EU/US data residency needs and customers asking for keys in our HSM.
[02:50] Rohit Patel: Yes, we need to confirm KMS provider compatibility. We use an on-prem HSM for some PII workflows, so we'd want to know whether Redwood Private supports HSM-backed keys or if we can bring our key material.
[03:05] Priya Nair: We support customer-managed keys in Private deployments and there's a KMS integration doc. I'll attach it in Slack; occasionally we see the doc title mis-typed — "KMS bring-your-own" — but it's there.

[03:35] Maya Singh: Timeline: ideally pilot starts week of 11/2 with go-live target in mid-November if pilot goes well. Is that realistic?
[03:50] Ava Martinez: That feels ok. We'll need your qps telemetry and the security questionnaire back by 10/26 to hit an 11/2 pilot start.

[04:10] Eli Mercer: Quick question on costs: can you share an initial sizing? We have a mix of long prompts (1k tokens) and short replies (80 tokens), curious about caching impact.
[04:25] Priya Nair: Sure. For mixed seq lengths we typically recommend enabling prefix/K-V cache for the long prompts to reduce repeated compute. Note, transcription quirk: sometimes our docs say K-V 'cash' in the export, but it's K-V cache. The cache hit rate will strongly influence token cost.
[04:45] Dana Zhou: For KV cache TTL, do you recommend per-customer or global? We have multi-tenant routing and can't have cross-tenant leaks.
[04:58] Priya Nair: Per-tenant only. Redwood's runtime isolates KV cache by tenant and model variant. We'll add the explicit note in the runbook.

[05:20] Jonas Park: On observability, we provide token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We'll need to add Sandbar's route names and tags so you can map cost to product features.
[05:35] Eli Mercer: Great. Also, can Redwood show canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models when capacity is constrained?
[05:47] Ava Martinez: Yes — rollouts (we call them cannery in some internal notes, ha) support canary percent and automatic fallback. We'll show the demo in the infra deep-dive.

[06:15] Rohit Patel: Regarding audit logs, does Redwood provide immutable logs for model invocations and admin actions? Retention policy?
[06:30] Jonas Park: We provide audit logs with configurable retention, and for Private there are options to push logs into your SIEM. Default retention for hosted is 90 days, but enterprise can request extended retention.
[06:45] Rohit Patel: Can logs be forwarded to our Splunk instance?
[06:50] Priya Nair: Yes, via syslog/HTTPS forwarding. We'll include a Splunk forwarder example in the security doc.

[07:15] Maya Singh: Pilot scope question — do you recommend we do a synthetic perf benchmark or run a shadow/test traffic pass on our preprod?
[07:30] Priya Nair: Both. Start with synthetic to validate the model and runtime with your seq-length distribution, then run a short shadow pass to observe real telemetry. We'll provide the benchmark harness (script + example dataset).
[07:45] Eli Mercer: Will we be able to test streaming responses in the pilot? Our chat UI depends on chunked streaming for perceived latency.
[07:55] Priya Nair: Yes, streaming is supported on both Hosted and Dedicated. Private supports it too but the network egress and TLS settings sometimes affect chunk sizes — we'll test that in the deep dive.

[08:20] Dana Zhou: Network question: for Private we're likely to host in our VPC. Any specific NAT or egress constraints we should be aware of?
[08:30] Ava Martinez: Private needs bi-directional control-plane connectivity during setup; after that you can lock down egress per policy. We'll provide the VPC peering/privatelink requirements. Sometimes the doc references Shared VPC incorrectly as "shard VPC" in transcriptions, just FYI.

[09:05] Jonas Park: On billing/commits — Dedicated is a reserved capacity model with monthly commit. We can model cost scenarios once we have expected qps and token mix.
[09:20] Eli Mercer: We're risk-averse on cost. If Dedicated has sudden cost jumps during campaign spikes, we need autoscaling with predictable burst pricing.
[09:33] Priya Nair: Autoscaling can be configured with capped burst capacity to limit cost exposure. We'll propose a baseline+dimmer burst policy.

[10:00] Maya Singh: Are there any known model variants Redwood recommends for multi-turn chat with emphasis on safety and instruction following? We also care about hallucinations.
[10:15] Priya Nair: There's a model catalog; for conversational use cases we recommend the 'conversational-stable' family (note: internal shorthand sometimes shows up in transcriptions as "converse-stable"). We'll also run evals with your prompt set to watch for regressions.

[10:45] Rohit Patel: Security nit: do you do fresh model weights scanning or vetting for third-party models loaded into the runtime?
[10:55] Priya Nair: We run a onboarding checklist for third-party models — checks include license verification, checksum validation, and runtime isolation. We'll share that checklist.

[11:20] Ava Martinez: Ok let's talk deliverables. We'll send a short onboarding runbook that includes required telemetry (qps, token hist, route names), security questionnaire, and an initial sizing spreadsheet.
[11:35] Eli Mercer: Good. For the sizing spreadsheet, include an example of how batching and KV cache hit rate flow into cost per 1k tokens, please.
[11:45] Jonas Park: We'll add columns for median/p95/p99 latencies, tokens per request, and estimated cost at 50/70/90% cache hit rates.

[12:10] Maya Singh: I want to make sure stakeholders are looped in. Who from Redwood will be our day-to-day contacts?
[12:18] Ava Martinez: Jonas is your CS contact. Priya will run technical items. I'll oversee commercial and help unblock procurement.
[12:25] Jonas Park: I'll set up a Slack channel and share calendar invites for the deep dive.

[12:40] Eli Mercer: Procurement question — what's the procurement lead time for Dedicated? We need to know legal and contract steps.
[12:50] Ava Martinez: Typical procurement for Dedicated (with SLA and enterprise terms) is 3–6 weeks depending on negotiation; for a pilot we can do a short-term contract or evaluation credits to start while redlining. We'll loop in Legal as needed.

[13:10] Rohit Patel: On compliance — do you have SOC 2 or ISO reports we can review?
[13:18] Jonas Park: Yes, we can share SOC 2 Type II and a summary compliance pack. We'll provide a redacted report link and an NDA-protected folder if needed.

[13:40] Maya Singh: Anything else from the product side — rollout plan for gradual traffic ramp?
[13:48] Priya Nair: We'll propose a 3-step ramp: synthetic bench -> shadow traffic -> canary traffic at 5/20/100%. We'll instrument circuit breakers and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency degrades.

[14:10] Eli Mercer: A practical item: our on-call wants to know what alerts they'll see. Can you share alert thresholds (latency, error rate, cost anomalies)?
[14:22] Jonas Park: We'll send a recommended alerting playbook including alerts for CPU/GPU saturation, queue depth, p95 latency, and token burn anomalies.

[14:45] Dana Zhou: For the infra deep-dive, I want to invite our networking SME and our infra SRE — can we make that a 60–90 minute session?
[14:55] Priya Nair: Yes, make it 90 minutes to cover VPC, egress, certs, and a short perf run. Proposed date in metadata.

[15:20] Maya Singh: Are there any gotchas with rolling updates to model weights and KV cache invalidation? Our product teams will push model updates fairly frequently.
[15:30] Priya Nair: We support version pinning and staged rollouts. KV cache invalidation can be configured per-deploy and we recommend a TTL plus explicit invalidation step during a major model switch. We'll document the ops runbook.

[15:55] Rohit Patel: Last sec: data retention for prompt/response logs used for evals — default is 90 days but can be reduced/masked?
[16:05] Jonas Park: Yes, you can mask or redact PII before logs land in our analytics pipeline; for Private you can choose to keep logs in your account only. We'll include masking examples.

[16:30] Ava Martinez: Quick recap of next steps — I'll send runbook + sizing + pricing bands; Priya will prepare config recs and deep-dive deck; Dana will share qps/histogram; Rohit returns security questionnaire. We'll aim to start pilot week of 11/2.
[16:50] Eli Mercer: Sounds good. Appreciate the clarity.
[16:55] Maya Singh: Thanks everyone.
[16:58] Jonas Park: I'll drop the action-items into the CRM and share calendar invites.
[17:05] Ava Martinez: Thanks all — recording ends.

Notes and docs referenced:
